subject: Cluster tenancy, RAID approach & PV quota ramp — GreenRiver air-gapped deployment
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.example.com>
To: Sam Ortega <ops@greenriver.example.com>, Lina Park <devops@greenriver.example.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.example.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Sep 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cluster tenancy, RAID approach & PV quota ramp — GreenRiver air-gapped deployment

Hi Sam / Lina —

Thanks for the intake call yesterday. As we start the on-prem plan for the air-gapped Kubernetes cluster, I want to align on three things we need decisions on before we finalize the runbook and PV quota schedule:

1) Tenancy model + node pool layout (how many node pools, roles, taints/tolerations, namespace mapping)
2) Persistent storage approach (local NVMe vs blockstore, RAID strategy, encryption, snapshot/backup constraints in air-gapped mode)
3) PV quota ramp and eviction policy (how we'll increment namespace quotas during onboarding to avoid large-scale OOM/evictions)

Quick asks from our side so we can size and produce the final BOM and acceptance tests:
- Expected per-tenant active dataset (GB/TB) and retention window for primary working set.
- Expected read/write IOPS profile (e.g., steady 1k IOPS, bursts to 20k for model prep loads).
- Tolerance for single-disk failure and RPO/RTO expectations for stateful services.
- Whether KMS integration is required for disk-level encryption (on-site HSM or Redwood-managed key material is not possible for air-gapped).

Our preliminary recommendation (attached PV quota proposal and RAID options):
- Use dedicated storage node pool with local NVMe for ephemeral/low-latency KV caches (explicitly tainted for cache workloads).
- Use a BlockStore-backed CSI class for long-lived model artifacts and DB volumes (replicated at blockstore layer).
- For on-node redundancy: prefer mdadm RAID1 for critical volumes + periodic snapshots to a removable archive (given air-gap constraints).
- Implement namespace-level ResourceQuotas and LimitRanges aligned to the PV quota ramp plan (attached spreadsheet).

Can you confirm the dataset sizes and whether you have a preferred RAID/fs (ZFS/mdadm/LVM) baseline? If you'd like, Karthik can outline a concrete PV size/IOPS schedule by tenant next.

Attachments: pv_quota_ramp_proposal_v1.xlsx, raid-storage-options_v2.pdf

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Infra Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Cluster tenancy, RAID approach & PV quota ramp — GreenRiver air-gapped deployment

Irene — thanks, this looks good as a starting point. A few clarifications from our side:

- Primary datasets: 6TB active model artifacts per tenant (we expect 3 tenants initially) with 90-day retention on hot tier; archive to offline NFS quarterly.
- IOPS profile: steady ~2k read, 500 write with bursts to 15k during nightly training prep.
- Failure tolerance: we can accept single-disk failure with 1–2 hour rebuild; cross-rack disk replacement could take up to 8 hours.
- Encryption: we require at-rest encryption using our on-prem KMS appliance (HSM). Redwood should provide guidance for integrating the CSI driver with the KMS; we will not share keys.

On RAID/fs: our ops prefer ZFS on NVMe for snapshotting, but we understand ZFS may complicate CSI workflows. If mdadm + ext4/xfs with periodic block-level snapshots to the archive is easier, we're open.

We attached a site network diagram and infra inventory (separate link). Next step for us: please propose a node-pool and PV quota ramp that fits these numbers so we can review with infra.

Thanks,
Sam Ortega
Head of Ops — GreenRiver Labs

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.example.com>
To: Sam Ortega <ops@greenriver.example.com>, Lina Park <devops@greenriver.example.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.example.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Sep 2029 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cluster tenancy, RAID approach & PV quota ramp — GreenRiver air-gapped deployment

Hi Sam / Lina —

Thanks for the details — below is a focused proposal that maps to your constraints and keeps the acceptance tests minimal for the first on-site validation. I'm calling out explicit numbers so the PV quota spreadsheet can be updated.

1) Node pool & tenancy layout
- control-plane (3 nodes, dedicated, no user pods)
- infra/system (3 nodes, kube-system, monitoring, logging, CSI controllers)
- storage-nodes (4 nodes to start; each with 4 x 3.84TB NVMe, used for PVs)
- compute-inference (6 nodes, GPUs/accelerators as required)
- compute-batch (3 nodes, CPU heavy for preprocessing)

Taints & namespace mapping: storage-nodes tainted: node-role.storage=only:NoSchedule. Namespaces with stateful workloads get tolerations plus annotation to bind to BlockStore CSI class. Cache namespaces use local-nvme storage class with node affinity.

2) Storage approach & RAID
- For your hot model artifacts (6TB per tenant): provision BlockStore-backed PVs (replicated at blockstore level) sized 8TB each to allow headroom; CSI will present the block device to the pod.
- For low-latency KV caches: local NVMe with local PersistentVolumes (CSI-local) and a StorageClass "local-nvme-fast" (reclaimPolicy: Delete, topology aware). Use this only for caches that can be rebuilt from upstream.
- RAID: where durability is required on a single node (e.g., local disk used to host an embedded DB that cannot be rehydrated), we recommend mdadm RAID1 across two NVMe devices per node. Rationale: predictable rebuild behavior, familiar maintenance model, and simplicity for site ops.
- ZFS: acceptable, but ZFS on top of a CSI-exposed block device complicates snapshot integration for Kubernetes backups. If GreenRiver prefers ZFS, plan to expose raw disks to a small set of storage VMs that run ZFS and export via CSI/Block. This increases operational surface area.

3) Encryption & KMS
- Use in-cluster CSI secrets that reference your on-prem KMS endpoints. We'll provide a template for the CSI driver key-provider hook. Keys remain on your HSM; Redwood will not hold keys for air-gapped sites.

4) PV quota ramp & eviction policy (concrete schedule)
- T0 (Week 0): Namespace quota per tenant = 2TB PV capacity, resourceQuota CPU=1000m per namespace, mem=4Gi.
- T1 (Week 2): bump to 4TB, CPU 2v, mem 8Gi after smoke tests and one simulated OOM window.
- T2 (Week 4): bump to 8TB (target), CPU 4v, mem 16Gi.
- At each ramp step run: fio profile (read/write mixed) with eviction window monitoring; ensure kubelet eviction thresholds set (evictionHard: memory.available<200Mi, nodefs.available<10%).

5) Acceptance tests we will run on-site
- Allocate 8TB PV to tenant namespace and run model load that simulates 15k IOPS bursts for 30 mins.
- Kill one NVMe device on storage node and validate rebuild within 2 hours to meet RTO.
- Validate KMS integration for attach/detach.

Attachments referenced: pv_quota_ramp_proposal_v1.xlsx (Irene's base; I'll add the ramp numbers), raid-storage-options_v2.pdf (detailed trade-offs).

If that looks good, Marissa and I will draft the final runbook and a preflight checklist for the on-site engineers.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
